s1.syndrome_frame: Bilateral ocular inflammation with recent onset of blurred vision and ocular irritation, following a systemic illness with fever and arthralgia
salient_findings: Stromal immune ring formation with underlying keratic precipitates
Positive Chikungunya virus PCR result in aqueous tap
key_facts: Patient is a teenage girl from Saint-Martin
Presented with bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Experienced fever and severe arthralgia one month earlier
Neurological complications are present
Periorbital hyperpigmentation is present
Ocular history is negative for trauma and previous inflammation
Primary HIV infection, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, and syphilis have been ruled out
Best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 OU
Slitlamp biomicroscopy revealed bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography confirmed localized anterior stromal infiltrate
Aqueous tap PCR result is positive for Chikungunya virus
IgM CHIKV serologic test is positive

raw.rationale: The presence of bilateral punctate superficial keratitis, stromal immune ring formation, and localized anterior stromal infiltrate confirmed by anterior segment optical coherence tomography, along with the positive PCR result for Chikungunya virus, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: anterior uveitis
rejected.why: While there is a mild anterior chamber reaction, the primary findings suggest a corneal rather than uveal involvement.

rejected.label: uveitis
rejected.why: Uveitis is a broader term that encompasses anterior uveitis, and the specific findings point more towards a corneal condition.

rejected.label: choroiditis
rejected.why: The normal fundus examination does not support choroiditis, which would affect the posterior segment of the eye.

rejected.label: scleritis
rejected.why: There is no indication of scleral inflammation, which is a hallmark of scleritis.
